records.name: Here
records.prompt:
Use case: logo-brand. Design ONE exceptionally minimal and distinctive PRIMARY LOGO for Little Stone Still Here (LSSH), a thoughtful personal website about learning, art, music and the lasting presence of its author, nicknamed Little Stone. This is a serious graphic identity study, not an illustration. The user's essential demand: an immediately memorable, extremely simple silhouette with a real conceptual reason for every part. Disciplined geometry, optical balance, confident proportions, warm restraint. At most two or three geometric parts, broad clear negative spaces, almost diagrammatically simple, but expertly judged like a cultural institution identity. Crisp planar vector-style shapes, exactly one uniform off-white ink on an absolutely flat pure black background. Absolutely no texture, highlights, bevels, shading, material, 3D, shadows or gradients. No fluid lobes, squishy organic shapes, beans, pickles, seeds, yin-yang swirls, ribbons, leaves, generic tech swooshes, spirals, elaborate interlocking ligatures, decorative letter crests or complex emblems. Tiny corner softening is allowed, no inflated pillowy geometry. Square composition, one logo centered at about 45% canvas width, generous even negative space. No sheets, alternatives, presentation layout, captions, titles or application mockups. No text except where the concept explicitly calls for letterforms. The logo must work by its shape even without explanatory copy. Do not reference or copy an existing brand.
CONCEPT 01 — THE PLACE AND THE STONE. Develop an exceptionally reduced graphic using one grounded, compact L-shaped architectural form and one small solid square stone tucked into its open interior. The L is both the initial of Little and a place to remain; the small separate square is the person still there. Only two parts. The enclosing L and the small square must feel inseparable as a unique optical unit, not a bracket and a bullet placed randomly. Use a short horizontal footing, one tall vertical, slightly eased square corners, a calm near-square overall footprint. Carefully tuned asymmetric spacing is the distinctive feature. This should have the clarity of a carved personal seal without a containing border. No letter text. Avoid a generic crop mark: the small stone must be meaningfully placed and the L must have substantial, beautiful proportions.
